chapter_title: The Human is less than all the Things of the Unive

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
When he came into a state where living truth flowed through the center of his understanding, he rejected the persuasion of merely outward life. He perceived that if the whole sufficient series of outer expressions arising from the natural self were brought up out of the deepest obscurity into the outermost plane, and if they were assembled into one seeming unity and arranged into a coherent order there, they would still not attain anything of what is truly elevated in the Lord. They could not be raised into the same interior degree, nor be extended into the same fullness, nor be opened into the same breadth, nor be brought down into the same complete ultimate, because they do not have the Divine quality within them.

And not only so: even if every one of those outer expressions, from the least to the greatest, were gathered into one general mass of knowledges and made to appear as a single comprehensive whole, they would still be absorbed into that generality, and their distinct form would perish there, as though extinguished in the merely natural plane. Yet within the natural plane there can still be many elevated states made great in outward form; and in their better condition these do not rise up against the holy stillness of Divine order, and they do not speak denial against the wisdom that enlightens, nor against the Divine power that holds all things together, nor against the Divine reality that is manifest through all things and gives them their total form, nor against the goods that proceed from righteousness; and in that better condition they do not invent an origin of evil in the Divine.

But the self-exalting principle of ruined humanity, which sets up what is unlike the Divine as though it were equal to Divine power and Divine being, was judged evil by the Lord of all. It spoke denial against the Divine power that supports the whole and against holy wisdom that gives light, and it violated Divine intelligence in its glory, and from that violation it produced the source of sin. From this came the blasphemous persuasion that every shameful evil and every defilement—every dominant evil, every hellish persuasion, every destroying lust, and every adversarial falsity—comes from the Divine, as though the Lord had established them from the beginning; yet they do not come from him, and this is a falsified witness against the Divine.

The Lord did not enter into the outermost degree and restore it for the sake of the human race alone, but in order to make manifest in ultimates what is powerful beyond ultimates, and to bring the whole expanse of created degrees into right order. When he finished his work in the outermost degree of universal life, he advanced further, conjoining the first formed good and the first formed truth to himself, and unveiling to them what had been hidden. In the same way he continually sent those who would teach to those capable of receiving good, age after age, and he disclosed to them a sufficient set of great essentials.

He opened to them the ordered successions of heavenly states and the manner in which they come forth, and he also taught the mode by which obscurity and falsity are permitted to exist. He announced to them the greatness of Divine wisdom, how it has acted against the strength of falsity and has overcome it. He taught that he entered into the state of spiritual death that reigns in the merely natural self, until he found what could be helped, and lifted them out of the lowest captivity in which they had been held.

All who are faithful and who inwardly acknowledge this truth receive spiritual life from three great and mighty essentials.

paragraph_translations.notes: The three essentials are not supplied in this excerpt, so they cannot be translated further.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coheres as a single teaching contrasting the insufficiency of merely external/natural formations with Divine elevation, then condemning the falsity that attributes evil to the Divine, and finally describing the Lord’s restorative work across all degrees and the essentials revealed through teaching. The main stumble is ¶3, where the damaged source text forces a best-fit synthesis; the ending promises three essentials without listing them, leaving the conclusion intentionally incomplete.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential teaching using an impossible comparison to establish disproportion between “words of the flesh” and a higher reality. No clear narrative break; the difficulty is lexical (“five words of the flesh”), not structural.
findings.evidence: Text: “five wo[r]ds of the f]lesh… gathered together… like [a single body]… lifted up to the heights… they will neither come to breadth… width… depth.” The spiritual reading notes only that “Five words of the flesh resists precision,” but it can still derive meaning by function (external utterance/form cannot reach the dimensions of the ‘mountain’/higher degree). The paragraph is internally consistent: gather → order → compare measures → fail to match.

findings.diagnosis: Damaged and internally dislocated transmission rather than a clean doctrinal insertion. The paragraph contains at least two broken similes spliced together (sea-drowning and mountains-on-earth) and several syntactic fractures that force the spiritual reading to ‘best-fit’ a single line. The stumble is caused by corruption/ellipses, not by an administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: Text shows repeated resets and non-sequiturs: “a single sea… [whole depth] that [s]ea… swallowed an[drowned]… [their form is destroyed]… they are in [this] earth [yet on] many [m]ountains… [and even if there is] sea in it,” then abruptly shifts to a moral-theological denial of blasphemy: “they did not guard against him… the silence… [do not oppose]… blasphemed hi[m] not… nor… utter blasphemies… [They attribute]… no cause of evil after Go[d].” The spiritual reading explicitly reports forcing coherence: “The paragraph is textually broken… the sequence about being on the earth/on many mountains is forced into a coherent spiritual line.” That is the signature of damage/fragmentary stitching rather than a voice-boundary insertion (no jurisdiction lists, no ranks, no named administrators).

findings.diagnosis: Coherent moral-theological polemic continuous with the end of ¶3 (“no cause of evil after God”). The ‘rulers/demons/fiends/satans’ are not administrative jurisdictions here; they function as classes of evil beings invoked to deny a false theodicy. No narrative break, only heightened rhetoric.
findings.evidence: Text: “idol of ill-fated human[it]y… blasphemed against the power… profaned… bringing forth the cause of every sin… rulers and the demons and the fiends and the satans… they say that they have come from God… they give false testimony about him.” The spiritual reading’s move (“multiple evil agents rendered as classes”) matches a functional/polemical use: the point is causal attribution (what evil is said to come from), not governance (who rules which station). This continues the prior line: denial that evil originates in God → condemnation of the doctrine that it does.

findings.diagnosis: Mixed voice: a likely seam where christological-historical narration (“Jesus… Adam and Eve… apostles”) has been fitted onto an earlier functional teaching about universal restoration/revelation. The spiritual reading had to “functionalize” the named figures to keep the correspondential story flowing, indicating a textual overlay rather than organic functional exposition.
findings.evidence: Text begins with a broad functional aim that fits correspondential teaching: “Jesus did not come… because of mankind alone… revealed… outside in the great expanse… finished doing his task outside in the great universe.” Then it narrows into named salvation-history actors: “he went… with Adam and Eve… sent the apostles… generation by generation,” and introduces a numbered catechesis: “revealed to them five great things.” The spiritual reading flags the tell: “Named figures are functionalized: ‘Adam and Eve’ as first formed good and first formed truth; ‘apostles’ as those sent to teach.” That functionalization is compensatory; the text itself presents administration-by-mission (sending apostles) and salvation-history sequencing rather than correspondence by function.
findings.scope: Annotate ¶7 as a probable redactional seam where salvation-history and mission language (Jesus/Adam & Eve/apostles, generational transmission) overlays or reframes an underlying universal/functional restoration teaching.

findings.diagnosis: Clean enumerative teaching with minimal narrative friction: a list of revealed ‘things’ (aeons/darkness; light versus darkness; descent to the province of death). While list-like, it is not administrative (no ranks/jurisdictions); it remains doctrinal and can be read functionally (how realities occur/act).
findings.evidence: Text: “He unveiled… about the aeons… how they occur… manner of the darkness, how it too exists… light… active against… conquered… came to the province of death… rules in the body.” The spiritual reading reports no stumbling here (“Clean” at ¶10; ¶11 explained smoothly). The items are explanatory-by-operation (“how they occur,” “active… conquered,” “came… until… bring them out”), not governance lists.

findings.diagnosis: Truncated ending / missing continuation rather than insertion. It promises “three great mighty things” but the excerpt does not supply them, producing an incomplete closure that the spiritual reading correctly notes as unsatisfied.
findings.evidence: Text: “All the faithful who believe this tr[u]th shall live by three great mighty things.” Spiritual reading: “The three essentials are not supplied in this excerpt… conclusion intentionally incomplete.” This is a classic sign of lacuna/excerpting: a forward-reference without the enumerated content.

textual_criticism.summary: 6 findings total. Two places where the spiritual reading stumbled are best explained by textual condition, not doctrinal intrusion: ¶3 is internally dislocated/damaged, and ¶13 is truncated. One likely redactional seam is ¶7, where salvation-history naming and mission transmission overlay a more universal functional teaching; recommend annotation (not excision) because the whole paragraph is the mixed boundary rather than a clean removable administrative list. No clear cases here warrant excision.

He [sa]ys: If one of all these five wo[r]ds of the f]lesh [should appear] today on the surfaces of the earth [were gathered together] out from [the abyss] which is deep. They will make it like [a single body] and they set them in order [and they set them in order]ne another, one [wi]th one upon the earth. They all [will be lifted] up to the heights against the elevation of this mountain [in proportion to] its height; they will neither come to breadth corresponding to [its] breadth, nor to width corresponding to its width, [nor to] depth corresponding to its depth.

Not only this, b[but each] one, all of them from their smallest to their g[greatest] a single sea [and were brought into] single [a] but [whole depth] that [s]ea and they are swallowed an[drowned] is in it [their form is destroyed] they are in [this] earth [yet on] many [m]ountains [and even if there is] sea in it, they [they stand forth] are very [gre]at in their fa[fashion, but]hey did not guard against him [in their better condition] the silence and they [do not oppose] blasphemed hi[m] not, neither against his l[igh]t that is displayed, no[r] do they utter blasphemies [a]gainst his power that supports the totality, nor against the [e]ssence that is displayed indicating the totality, [nor] against the good works of righteousness. [They attribute]count no cause of evil after Go[d].

However, [the i]dol of ill-fated human[it]y [set itself up] the one that will be unlike anything, that is equal [to the power and the essence] great works; and it was found evil [by] God, the Lord of all. It even blasphemed again[st the] power that supports the totality, against its hol[y] light; [and it] profaned its glorious wisdom, bringing forth the cause of every sin. They say that every disgraceful wickedness and defilement, the rulers and the demons and the fiends and the satans, they say that they have come from God, that he is the one who [es]tablished them [in the beginning] they came not from him, and they give false testimony about him.

Jesus did not come and s[a]ve the world because of mankind alone, but [but when he] came and revealed on earth [what was strong] was strong outside in [the great expanse] And [whe]n he had finished doing his [t]ask outside [i]n the great u[ni]verse, he came [and when he went]t further with Adam and Eve and revealed [to them]. Even so, he sent the apostles to the good, [g]enera- tion by generation, and revealed to them five great thin[gs].
[Se]cond: He unveiled to them about the aeons [of the greatness], how they occur; and he taught them about [the manner of] the darkness, how it t[o]o exists.
[The th]ird time: He proclaimed to them about the [l]ight great-[ness], how it has been active against the pow[er of] darkness and conquered it.

Fourth: He taught them that he came to the province of death [that rules in the body] that is flesh, until he should find profit and bring them from the gate of the underworld below, for [they had] been swa[ll]owed into it.
All the faithful who believe this tr[u]th shall live by three great mighty things.

changes_summary: No changes made. The critic issued no excisions: Findings 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 recommend none, and Finding 4 recommends annotate (not text modification).
